purpose: Resolve the next adversarial fog: the expeditionary contractor state, the commercial-innovation bridge, flexible acquisition scaling, the bounded Palantir I2-to-I3 sequence, and the exact identity of ICE's detention-and-release risk-classification system. The wave records affirmative support and bounded non-links with equal force.

method.null_hypothesis: ordinary institutional adaptation, lawful commercial acquisition, and independent system development
method.promotion_rule: A phase, mechanism, or system proposition may be supported for human review only at the scope established by the operative record. Temporal succession is not causation; one vendor lane is not a coordinated network; a system identity non-link must be preserved even when it weakens the thesis.
method.source_rule: GAO records are official institutional evidence. A published appellate opinion is used as a judicially described system map based on the agency record; a public opinion mirror does not substitute for future custody of the official PDF.

records.proposition: The post-2001 expeditionary state relied extensively on contractors for military, reconstruction, security, logistics, and support functions while lacking complete personnel and oversight data.

sources.title: Contingency Contracting: DOD, State, and USAID Contracts and Contractor Personnel in Iraq and Afghanistan

records.observation: GAO found extensive contractor reliance in Iraq and Afghanistan, at least $33.9 billion in reported obligations across almost 57,000 contracts during the reviewed 18-month period, and 197,718 DOD contractor personnel as of April 2008. GAO also found incomplete, unreliable, or absent personnel-tracking and casualty data across the agencies.
supports: P2 expeditionary-contractor state as an institution-level historical condition
large-scale substitution of contracted capacity for public operating capacity
dispersed responsibility and incomplete oversight as documented administrative consequences
does_not_support: a single contractor or network controlling the expeditionary state
continuity from a named P2 contractor into a present platform
intentional opacity rather than administrative failure
capture, coercion, or private extraction
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire function-level contract, command, systems-integration, data, performance, insourcing, termination, and successor records that show which contracted capacities persisted into P3 institutions.
records.falsifier: Complete function and workforce denominators show contractor use was temporary, noncritical, readily reversible, and did not displace or weaken durable public capacity.

records.proposition: DOD institutionalized a commercial-technology translation and selection bridge through the Defense Innovation Unit and its flexible award process.

sources.title: Defense Innovation Unit: Actions Needed to Assess Progress and Further Enhance Collaboration

records.observation: GAO states that DOD created DIU in 2015 to accelerate commercial-technology adoption, that DIU developed a flexible award process, and that from fiscal years 2016 through 2023 it made 450 prototype awards. DIU reported that 62 prototype agreements, or 51 percent of projects with at least one completed prototype, transitioned to production; prototype obligations were about $1.7 billion and reported transition ceilings exceeded $5.5 billion.
supports: P3 innovation bridge as a formal institution rather than a narrative label
a public selector and translator between commercial companies and military users
prototype-to-production conversion as an observable institutional process
does_not_support: that selected firms were chosen through a recurring private network
that every transition succeeded operationally
that ceilings equal obligations or outlays
that DIU narrowed options improperly
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Freeze every DIU applicant, eligible company, award, completed prototype, transition, nontransition, production obligation, user, selector, investor, and unsuccessful path by year and problem area.
records.falsifier: Complete denominators show DIU did not materially alter commercial access, selection, prototype conversion, or production adoption relative to ordinary acquisition channels.

records.proposition: DOD scaled flexible prototype acquisition after 2016 and used it extensively to bring nontraditional companies into defense acquisition.

sources.title: Defense Acquisitions: DOD's Use of Other Transactions for Prototype Projects Has Increased

records.observation: GAO found that DOD's use of prototype other transactions increased significantly from fiscal years 2016 through 2018 and that nontraditional companies participated to a significant extent in 88 percent of the transactions awarded during that period. GAO also found two reviewed transactions that lacked required higher-level review before award.
supports: a dated P3-to-P4 acquisition-mechanism transition
institutional opening to nontraditional commercial suppliers
the simultaneous need for controls and review as acquisition flexibility expanded
does_not_support: a founder-controlled option set
improper awards generally
production success or institutional replacement
a causal link to any named present-day platform
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Enumerate prototype and production other transactions, participants, consortia, intermediaries, review exceptions, transitions, failures, competition states, and later operating dependence.
records.falsifier: Complete transaction records show no meaningful increase, no broader commercial participation, or no persistent effect on production pathways and supplier selection.

records.proposition: A bounded Palantir-Army sequence runs from deliberate procurement-gate intervention through later competitive deployments to an enterprise agreement whose J&A describes institutional dependence.

sources.publisher: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit
sources.title: Palantir USG, Inc. v. United States, Appeal No. 17-1465
U.S. Army Awards Enterprise Service Agreement to Enhance Military Readiness and Drive Operational Efficiency
Palantir Enterprise Agreement award and J&A notice

records.observation: The Federal Circuit record establishes a deliberate commercial-item gate challenge without requiring Palantir's selection. Later Army records establish multiple deployments and a 2025 enterprise agreement; the associated J&A text describes growing dependence, proprietary integration, migration and reaccreditation costs, and continuity concerns.
supports: a bounded longitudinal I2-to-I3 sequence
the progression from gate-shaping action to later institutional operating position
a concrete actor-specific research chain across P3, P4, and P5
does_not_support: that the litigation caused the later enterprise position
that any award was improperly tailored
that Palantir designed the broader innovation regime
system-wide common purpose, coercion, or extraction
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire each intervening solicitation, evaluation, award, protest, acceptance, production transition, contract modification, operating responsibility, performance result, and alternative-provider record from 2016 through 2025.
records.falsifier: The intervening record shows independent requirements, broad competition, no durable advantage from the legal challenge, and enterprise consolidation explained entirely by later performance and ordinary acquisition decisions.

records.proposition: Palantir ICM is the ICE system that stores and executes detention-and-release Risk Classification Assessments.

sources.publisher: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit, public opinion reproduction
sources.title: ACLU Immigrants' Rights Project v. ICE, No. 21-1233

records.observation: The appellate opinion's agency-record description states that Risk Classification Assessment data are stored in the Risk Classification Assessment module of ICE's Enforcement Case Tracking System, which is stored in the Enforcement Integrated Database and not in the Integrated Decision Support System. It does not identify ICM as the RCA module or system.
supports: exact RCA system identity at the level described in the judicial record
a separate ECTS/EID consequence-system lane
rejection of the direct ICM-equals-RCA system shortcut
does_not_support: the absence of any ICM-derived input to ECTS or RCA
the absence of shared identifiers or data feeds
the fairness or accuracy of RCA decisions
a complete current architecture after the source period
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire the official opinion PDF, current EID/ECTS/RCA privacy and system records, contracts, interface diagrams, data lineage, module ownership, and change history; separately test any ICM-to-EID or ICM-to-RCA feed.
records.falsifier: Current operative records establish that ICE formally replaced the ECTS/EID RCA module with ICM or embedded RCA as an ICM module during the relevant consequence period.

records.proposition: ICE operates an event-centric, cross-stage data architecture capable of relating apprehension, risk assessment, detention, removal, and bond records to individual people through shared identifiers.

sources.publisher: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit, public opinion reproduction
sources.title: ACLU Immigrants' Rights Project v. ICE, No. 21-1233

records.observation: The opinion describes EID as ICE's common repository for records created, updated, and accessed by several applications, supporting case management from arrest or removal-proceeding entry through final disposition. It describes IIDS as a regularly updated EID snapshot for reporting, RCA as an ECTS module stored in EID, and A-Numbers as the cross-record key ICE can use for person-centric retrieval.
supports: L1-to-L6/H3 system architecture at an agency level
cross-stage relational capacity across immigration-enforcement events
a visibility and public-inspection issue caused by event-centric storage and identifier redaction
does_not_support: one vendor controlling the full architecture
automated decision-making
an ICM-to-RCA consequence chain
coercive ideology or private extraction
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire current system-of-record notices, PIAs, data dictionaries, module and vendor ownership, interface diagrams, role permissions, retention, audit, correction, FOIA production, and consequence-specific case lineage.
records.falsifier: Current system records show the described cross-stage relational architecture no longer exists or cannot produce person-level linkage across the relevant enforcement stages.

records.proposition: ICM data or analytics materially feed the ECTS/EID Risk Classification Assessment workflow.

sources.title: ICE J&A-25-0266 Investigative Case Management limited-sources notice

sources.publisher: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit, public opinion reproduction
sources.title: ACLU Immigrants' Rights Project v. ICE, No. 21-1233

records.observation: The ICM record establishes broad investigative data ingestion and case analytics; the judicial system map places RCA in ECTS/EID. The current bounded sources do not identify a specific ICM-derived field, analytic output, interface, or workflow input used by RCA.
supports: a precise interface question between two separately identified ICE systems
does_not_support: a material ICM-to-RCA data flow
Palantir causation of detention or release
automation or absence of human discretion
I4 coercive ideological governance
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire interface-control records, source-to-target field lineage, API or batch-transfer documentation, shared identifier use, role and workflow rules, audit logs, change requests, and case-level traces between ICM and ECTS/EID RCA.
records.falsifier: Architecture and operational records show no ICM-derived data, analytics, identifiers, alerts, or workflow outputs enter RCA or materially influence its users.

records.proposition: The repository's five-phase periodization is supported as an institution-level sequence from post-Cold War capacity retrenchment through expeditionary contracting, commercial-innovation bridges, flexible acquisition, and post-2022 scaling.

sources.title: High-Risk Series: Dedicated Leadership Needed to Address Limited Progress in Most High-Risk Areas
Contingency Contracting: DOD, State, and USAID Contracts and Contractor Personnel in Iraq and Afghanistan
Defense Acquisitions: DOD's Use of Other Transactions for Prototype Projects Has Increased
Defense Innovation Unit: Actions Needed to Assess Progress and Further Enhance Collaboration

records.observation: The combined official record supports a sequence of reduced acquisition capacity and contractor reliance, expeditionary contractor scale, formal commercial-innovation institutions, increased flexible prototype acquisition, and a 2023 DIU 3.0 shift toward delivering commercial technology at speed and scale for critical operational needs.
supports: the five phases as a defensible institution-level research periodization
observable changes in acquisition institutions and public-private operating mechanisms
phase-specific acquisition questions rather than a single timeless capture theory
does_not_support: one continuous centrally planned project
the same actors controlling every phase
causal continuity for a named company or founder network
capture, coercion, or extraction
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Build phase-boundary ledgers that identify the exact public capability, instrument, organization, personnel, contractor, technical baseline, rights holder, successor, and comparator crossing each transition.
records.falsifier: Phase-complete records show no durable change in public capacity, contractor dependence, commercial selection mechanisms, acquisition flexibility, or scaling institutions across the proposed boundaries.

records.proposition: The institution-level P1-to-P5 sequence establishes that one founder-controlled network deliberately designed and captured the full post-Cold War conversion architecture.
records.observation: The phase records establish institutional conditions and mechanisms. The Palantir lane establishes one actor-specific I2-to-I3 sequence. The records do not establish founder-network continuity across P1 and P2, common governance across firms and funds, a joint design process, or a complete authority-to-consequence-to-private-benefit chain.
supports: continued testing of bounded actor-specific phase crossings
does_not_support: continuous founder-network authorship from 1991 onward
joint design across companies, capital, banks, policy organizations, and agencies
a concealed transnational organism
I4 coercive governance or I5 extraction
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Require named P1/P2 predecessors, exact personnel and ownership continuity, shared strategy or governance, operative cross-entity instruments, two-sided transfers, consequential workflows, and causal private-benefit records.
records.falsifier: Complete phase and actor denominators show independent adaptation, ordinary labor and capital markets, no continuous governance or planning, effective competition, and no common operating design.
